historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-case 10-year revenue CAGR FY26->FY36 (~2.8%), trough-to-mid-cycle; no historical CAGR is usable because every 3-yr series measures FY23-peak to FY26-trough and every 5-yr series starts at the FY21 COVID trough
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR (+0.6%) diverges >30% from revenue 5-yr CAGR (+8.5%) and EPS 5-yr CAGR (-20.9%); 3-yr CAGRs are all negative and describe the FY24 peak to FY26 trough. Historical CAGRs are cycle artefacts, not a growth basis.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC - lease principal (treatment B): FY21 77.1, FY23 101.0, FY26 73.5 (AUD m). Owner-FCF 3-yr CAGR (-10.0%) is below reported (-7.7%) because SBC and lease cash held up while FCF fell. FY26 owner FCF is flattered by a working-capital release (DSO 36->34 days, contract assets down) and cash tax paid of only $16.7m; the component build, not the FY26 print, sets the forward margin.

scenario_narratives.base: Trough in FY27, gradual policy normalisation from FY28, mid-cycle 23% EBITDA margin by FY31, revenue back to the FY24 nominal peak only by FY36. Transformation spend charged as real cash. This is the 'IDP survives the policy cycle as the scale leader with a leaner cost base' path.
scenario_narratives.bull: Policy turns early (FY28), share gains from failed competitors, China IELTS and new destinations compound, margins recover to ~26% by FY31, just under the FY24 level. Buy-back accretion at ~A$2 is additional upside not in the number.
scenario_narratives.bear: Structural decline: permanent caps, IELTS share loss to PTE/Duolingo, agent disintermediation. Revenue bottoms ~$645m in FY29 and grows 2%; margin capped at 20%. The company remains cash-generative and solvent (net debt/EBITDA stays <1.5x), so this is a value-erosion bear, not a solvency bear.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF on a business at a policy-driven trough. The valuation does not extrapolate the FY26 decline or the FY22-24 boom; it charges restructuring as cash, deducts the full IFRS-16 lease charge, holds the count flat with SBC expensed, uses one AUD WACC across scenarios (risk lives in the flows and the 30% bear weight), and caps the terminal multiple at 15x owner FCF for a cyclical. The market price at ~3.8x FY26 adjusted EBITDA and ~10x adjusted EPS is pricing something close to the bear path; the question the model answers is what the equity is worth if IELTS co-ownership and the placement network survive the cycle at a lower margin than the peak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Visa/migration policy in Australia, Canada, UK and US does not normalise - the base case assumes recovery begins FY28; each additional year of decline is worth roughly $0.30-0.40/share
IELTS loses acceptance to PTE / Duolingo English Test faster than assumed (India Language Testing revenue -24% in FY26); the 24% mid-cycle margin assumes IELTS pricing holds
Transformation costs recur beyond FY29 (FY25 $7.6m, FY26 $36.2m, FY27 ~$40m): the base case tapers them out by FY29
Yield growth that cushioned FY26 (placement fee +10%) may reflect mix, not pricing power, and could reverse as volumes recover
FX: revenue in ~50 currencies, $21.3m FY26 translation headwind; AUD strength lowers AUD revenue and margin
Cash in FX-controlled jurisdictions and credit-loss provisions ($6.0m FY26, $15.1m FY25) recur; not haircut in the bridge

sanity_check_fix.tripped_on: Implied P/E 181.2x exceeds 2x the 10yr average 73.4x (sanity_check.py, first pass, base IV 3.49 over FY26 statutory EPS 4.4c less SBC/share = 1.9c)
sanity_check_fix.fix_applied: mid-cycle FCF (priority 1): terminal post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin trimmed 1pp in base (24% -> 23%, FY29-30 path lowered in step) and bull (27% -> 26%); bear unchanged at 20%. Base terminal owner-FCF margin falls from 10.8% to ~10.1% of revenue, inside the FY22-FY23 owner-FCF range (10.9%, 10.3%) rather than at its top. No WACC premium was stacked: risk is already charged once in the flows and the 30% bear weight (owner-fcf-adaptations (f)), and the diagnosis keywords (regulatory single point of failure, geographic concentration) are exactly what the bear scenario and its weight price.
sanity_check_fix.why_the_rule_cannot_clear: The P/E rule divides IV by FY26 statutory EPS of 4.4c, a trough print after $50.3m of significant items (restructuring 36.2, credit-loss 6.0, FX 3.2, remediation 2.7, M&A 2.2) on a $795m revenue base; less SBC/share the denominator is 1.9c. Clearing 2x the 10-yr average (146.8x) would require base IV below ~$2.83, i.e. pricing the trough year as permanent. On FY26 ADJUSTED EPS of 20.2c the base IV is ~16x and the weighted IV ~15x, BELOW the 10-yr historical P/E minimum of 24.6x; EV/EBITDA at IV is ~9x against a 10-yr average of 29x and minimum 6.4x; P/Sales 1.2x against an average of 6.1x. The valuation is not aggressive on any cycle-normalised multiple; the trip is a trough-denominator artefact and is recorded, not engineered away.
sanity_check_fix.result_after_fix: Still trips on P/E only (169.2x vs 146.8x threshold); P/B, EV/EBITDA and P/Sales pass. Base IV 3.49 -> 3.26, weighted 3.20 -> 3.03. One fix pass applied per the skill priority order; no further lever is applied because the remaining gap is the trough-EPS denominator, not the valuation (see why_the_rule_cannot_clear).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 22.4 / cash flow statement share-based payments add-back $6,864k; equity-award taxes nil (no net-share settlement withholding disclosed)
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted weighted average used for diluted EPS, FY2026 Annual Report note 7: 280,432,135. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so the count is not compounded. The $50m on-market buy-back approved 19 June 2026 is an authorisation, not a spend (FY26 financing outflow on shares: $1.8m); at ~A$2/share it could retire ~9% of the count, which is accretion NOT modelled here (buybacks are value-neutral in the house method).
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD-built. Australian 10-yr government bond ~4.4%, equity risk premium ~5.5%, beta ~1.2 for a policy-cycle-driven services business -> cost of equity ~11%; pre-tax cost of debt ~6.5% (bank facilities, 25.5m finance costs on ~254m drawn) on ~15% debt weight -> WACC ~10.0%. Risk is charged ONCE: cyclicality and the visa-policy dependency live in the scenario flows and the 30% bear weight, so the same 10% WACC is used in all three scenarios with no ad-hoc premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. The full IFRS-16 lease cash charge (FY26: principal $22.78m in financing + interest $6.32m in operating = $29.1m, 3.66% of revenue) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities ($81.4m at 30 June 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt; and da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation ($65.1m less $24.3m ROU = $40.8m, 5.1% of FY26 revenue) so the lease is not charged twice. last_fcf deducts lease principal from reported FCF (lease interest already sits inside OCF).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial ($1.4m book, $1.0m FY26 profit share, Cambodia/Taiwan schools). Charged once via a -$1.4m equity-bridge deduction at book; flows are left on a consolidated basis.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row: operating company, non-US, cyclical) with the owner-fcf-adaptations applied for AUD WACC, IFRS-16 leases (treatment B) and NCI. REASON: IDP is a fee-for-service operating company (Student Placement commissions, IELTS test fees) whose value is a stream of free cash flow; it is not a REIT, bank, LIC or shell. CYCLE POSITION: this is a trough build, not a run-rate build. Big-Four international student volumes fell ~54% over FY24-FY26 on coordinated visa tightening, FY26 revenue fell 11% to $795.4m, and management's FY27 Adjusted EBIT guidance of $95-115m is a third consecutive decline with no confirmed trough. Neither the FY26 decline nor the FY22-FY24 boom (revenue 793->1,037m, adjusted EBIT margin 18-23%) is extrapolated: the base case troughs revenue in FY27 (-7%), recovers to the nominal FY24 peak only by ~FY36, and lifts the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA margin from a transformation-cost-burdened 16% in FY27 to a 23% mid-cycle level (FY26 clean adjusted EBITDA margin 22.3%; FY22 22.8%; FY23-24 26.6-28.5% peak). EBITDA BASE: FY26 statutory EBITDA $126.9m + significant items $50.3m (credit-loss provision 6.0, restructuring 36.2, FX 3.2, remediation 2.7, M&A 2.2) = $177.2m adjusted, 22.3% of revenue. Restructuring is treated as a REAL cash cost, not an add-back: the ~$40m FY27 transformation/ERP spend (5.4pp of revenue) is charged inside the FY27 EBITDA margin and tapers through FY28-FY29. CASH TAX: 30% throughout (Australian statutory; FY16-FY22 cash tax rates 30-35%). The FY24-FY26 cash rates of 40-97% are artefacts of non-deductible significant items on a collapsing pre-tax base and are not a forward basis. FY2025 comparatives restated for Student Placement revenue recognition (revenue 882.2 -> 891.4, NPAT 44.5 -> 49.7); the CSV carries originally-reported FY2025 and the restated values sit in kpis (RevenueRestated, NetIncomeRestated). NET DEBT is the company's own definition (drawn bank loans $253.8m less cash $135.1m = $118.6m; FY26 AR p.23). Some cash in FX-controlled jurisdictions (e.g. Iran) may be slow to repatriate; not haircut. INTEREST INCOME ($4.3m) is not stripped because the company is net-debt and the cash is netted in the bridge, per the house rule. WORKING CAPITAL: wc_capture -3% (growth consumes cash) because Student Placement carries contract assets and receivables (DSO 34 days) that exceed the deferred-revenue balance; a flat 0 would be marginally generous.

bear.narrative: The FY24-26 decline is structural, not cyclical: Big-Four caps become the permanent settings, PTE and the Duolingo English Test keep taking IELTS acceptance (India Language Testing revenue already -24% in FY26), and digital platforms (ApplyBoard, Studylink) plus direct university recruitment disintermediate the counsellor model. Revenue falls a further 12% in FY27 and 6% in FY28, bottoming near $645m in FY29 before crawling at 2%. The fixed test-centre and counsellor base holds the EBITDA margin at 13-20%, and lease cash stays a larger share of a smaller revenue base. Terminal growth 1.5%; Gordon binds below the 15x cap.

base.narrative: FY27 revenue -7% (Adjusted EBIT guide $95-115m midpoint ~$105m on ~$740m revenue), with the ~$40m transformation/ERP spend charged inside a 16% EBITDA margin. Volumes stabilise in FY28 and recover 5-6%/yr FY29-FY31 as Australian caps ease (2026 cap +9% to 295k) and China IELTS, Malaysia/UAE placement and Student Essentials add non-Big-Four revenue; growth fades to 3% by FY34. Margin rebuilds to 23% by FY31 (trimmed from 24% in the sanity-check fix pass) on the $47m cost-out ($32m FY26 + $15m FY27) and operating leverage, below the FY23-24 peak of 26.6-28.5%. Revenue regains its FY24 nominal peak only in FY36.

bull.narrative: Policy cycle turns in FY28: Australia lifts caps further, Canada/UK stabilise, and IDP's quality positioning (visa approval rates above industry, NPS >70) wins share from weaker agents that did not survive the downturn. China IELTS scales from 13 centres. Yield growth persists (placement fee +10%, IELTS +2% in FY26). Margin reaches 26% by FY31 - just under the FY24 level of 26.6% and well below the FY23 peak (trimmed from 27% in the sanity-check fix pass) - and the $50m buy-back at ~A$2 retires ~9% of the count (not modelled; upside to this case).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 30% because the single largest driver of revenue - sovereign student-visa policy in four countries - is outside IDP's control, management itself guides a third consecutive year of volume decline with no confirmed trough, and two structural competitive threats (alternative English tests, digital agent platforms) run in parallel with the cycle. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (policy reversal, share gains AND China scale-up). Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.

diagnosis.detail: Structural risks in the qualitative analysis that a standard WACC may not price: regulatory single point of failure, geographic concentration
